chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih and Ubayd Allah al-Tawil, from a Sheikh from al-Nakha', who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I have not ceased to be a governor since the time of al-Hajjaj until this day of mine. So is there repentance for me?' He remained silent. Then I repeated it to him, so he said: 'No, until you repay to every rightful one his right.'

key_terms.الْحَجَّاجُ: Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, the famous Umayyad governor
key_terms.ذِي حَقٍّ: One who has a right (to compensation/dues)

ai.seo_question: What is required for complete repentance after serving as a governor under an unjust ruler?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights the distinction between spiritual repentance and social justice by remaining silent initially, signaling the gravity of the companion's prolonged service under the Umayyad tyrant al-Hajjaj. The Imam clarifies that true *tawbah* requires the restitution of specific rights (*huquq*) to those who were oppressed or owed dues, emphasizing that divine forgiveness is contingent upon settling debts to people before settling them with God.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Wahab Bin Abd Rabbih, and Ubeydullan Al Taweel, from a Sheykh from Al Nakha’a who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>: ‘I have not ceased to be a governor since the era of Al-Hajjaj up to this day of mine. So, is there a repentance for me?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> remained silent. Then I repeated unto him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until you repay to every rightful one, his right’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Wahab ibn ‘Abd Rabbihi and ‘Ubayd Allah al-Tawil from Shaykh from al-Nakha’ who has said the following: “

Once I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.) ‘I have been working as a governor from the time of al-Hajjaj to this time, can my repentance be accepted?’ The Imam remained quiet. I repeated my question and then he said, ‘No, until you pay back everything that you owe to the people.’”
